Albanian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Arabic إسلام.

[edit]

islam (feminine islame)

  1. Islamic

Noun

[edit]

islam m (definite islami)

  1. Islam

singular
indefinite definite

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Arabic إِسْلَام (ʔislām, “submission, surrender”), verbal noun of أَسْلَمَ (ʔaslama).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic, Valencia) [izˈlam]
  • Audio (Barcelona):(file)

Noun

[edit]

islam m (plural islams)

  1. Islam

Derived terms

[edit]
  • islàmic
  • islamisme
  • islamístic
  • islamita
  • islamitzar

Related terms

[edit]
  • muslim
  • musulmà

Further reading

[edit]
  • “islam”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007

[edit]

Pronunciation

  • Hyphenation: is‧lam

Noun

islam

Verb

islam

Maltese

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • iżlam

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian islam, from Arabic إسْلام (ʔislām). The related word mislem (“Muslim”) was inherited from Arabic, but all other terms are learned borrowings.

Preseded spelling of iżlam.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɪsˈlaːm/
  • Rhymes: -aːm

Noun

[edit]

islam m

  1. Islam (religion)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • islamiku

Related terms

[edit]
  • mislem
  • musulman

Polish

Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
islam
Wikipedia pl

Etymology

[edit]

Internationalism; compare English Islam, French islam, German Islam, ultimately from Arabic إسلام.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈi.slam/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -islam
  • Syllabification: i‧slam

Noun

[edit]

islam m inan (related adjective islamski or islamicki or islamiczny)

  1. Islam (monotheistic Abrahamic religion followed by Muslims that is based on the teachings of Muhammad and the Qur'an)
    Synonym: mahometanizm
